title: String Compression III
summary: Given a string word, repeatedly remove the longest prefix consisting of a single character that appears at most 9 times consecutively, record the length of this prefix followed by the character, and continue until the word is empty.
statement: Given a string word, repeatedly remove the longest prefix consisting of a single character that appears at most 9 times consecutively, record the length of this prefix followed by the character, and continue until the word is empty. Return the resulting compressed string.
constraints: word is a nonempty string of lowercase letters.
Encode each maximal run in left-to-right chunks containing at most nine equal characters.
For every chunk append its one-digit length followed by its character.
hints: A run longer than nine must be split even though its character does not change.
At each position extend only while the character matches and the chunk length remains below nine.
Emit length and character, then continue at the first unconsumed position.
Each iteration removes the longest legal prefix required by the specification, so concatenating emissions is deterministic.
editorial: Each iteration removes the longest legal prefix required by the specification, so concatenating emissions is deterministic.

tests.explanation: Each character forms a run of length one, producing 1a1b1c1d1e.
Fourteen a characters split into 9a and 5a, followed by 2b.
